# else over each atom-bearing union, a named family, the bare atom and a type with no atom.

template: $0 else 0
int | #none => error An `else` that does not name its atoms -- sec:failure "An `else` names every atom it takes ... A bare `e else d` ... is rejected in every position" (QUESTIONS A113)
int | #a | #b => error An `else` that does not name its atoms -- sec:failure "A bare `e else d` ... is rejected in every position" (QUESTIONS A113)
=#none => error An `else` that does not name its atoms -- sec:failure "A bare `e else d` ... is rejected in every position" (QUESTIONS A113)
int => error An `else` that does not name its atoms -- sec:failure "A bare `else` on such an `e` is rejected as every bare `else` is, and since `e` holds no loose atom to list, its repair is this menu" (QUESTIONS A67, A113)

template: $0 else #none -> 0
int | #none => int -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a` of `e`'s union type by `d`"; sec:type_resolution "Unions split, joins merge"
f64 | #none => 0 | f64 -- sec:type_resolution "Unions split, joins merge" ("if c { 1 } else { 2.5f64 } is 1 | f64")
rat | #none => 0 | rat -- sec:type_resolution "Unions split, joins merge"
=#none => 0 -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"; L1.26a "an integer literal is read as an int ... as the default after else" (a literal prints as it was written)
int => int warn !! L2.12e: int -- sec:failure "else with nothing to strip" (QUESTIONS A67)

template: $0 else #none -> 2.5f64
int | #none => int | f64 -- sec:type_resolution "Unions split, joins merge", no conversion
f64 | #none => f64 -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"

template: $0 else #none -> false
bool | #none => bool -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"

template: $0 else #none -> ""
Utf8String | #none => Utf8String !! STR-types: notyet -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"

template: $0 else #a -> 0
int | #a | #b => int | #b -- sec:failure "every other member of `e`'s type is kept"
f64 | #a => 0 | f64 -- sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"

template: $0 else #a -> 0 else #b -> 1
int | #a | #b => int -- sec:lexical "several pattern forms chain left to right"

template: ($0 + 1) else #none -> 0
int | #none => int -- sec:failure "an atom an operand carries in passes through"; sec:failure "`e else #a -> d` replaces the atom `#a`"
